articles.title: Renal Outcomes and Variant Effects in Monoallelic COL4A3/COL4A4-Related Alport Syndrome: A Single-Center Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Autosomal dominant Alport syndrome (AD-AS) is caused by pathogenic/likely pathogenic (P/LP) variants in COL4A3 and COL4A4. Its clinical spectrum ranges from isolated hematuria to proteinuric chronic kidney disease (CKD) eventually progressing to kidney failure (KF). We aimed to characterize the clinical and genetic profile of AD-AS in northwest Portugal, with particular focus on the recurrent COL4A3 c.1219G>C p.(Gly407Arg) variant. METHODS: We conducted an observational cohort study at a major university hospital. Eligible participants were heterozygous for COL4A3 or COL4A4 variants. Demographic, clinical, and genetic data were collected. Time to CKD≥3 and CKD5/KF was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Subcohorts were defined by gene, variant type, and variant of interest. RESULTS: A total of 218 individuals (16 children) from 123 families were included. Definitive molecular diagnosis was obtained in 75%. Among COL4A3 carriers, 117 had P/LP variants, predominantly missense; among COL4A4 carriers, 47 had P/LP variants, predominantly truncating. COL4A3 p.(Gly407Arg) represented 62% of COL4A3 P/LP variants and 44% of the patient cohort. History of microscopic hematuria was present in 93% of patients, whereas history of significant proteinuria was documented in 68% and hypertension in 48%. CKD≥3 developed in 33%, and 21% progressed to CKD5/KF. Proteinuria independently predicted CKD progression (p=0.001). Carriers of COL4A3 p.(Gly407Arg) had earlier onset of hypertension and higher prevalence of proteinuria than carriers of other COL4A3 P/LP variants. Glomerular basement membrane thinning was noted on electron microscopy in all biopsy specimens. Extrarenal manifestations were uncommon. CONCLUSIONS: Heterozygous COL4A3/4 P/LP variants are frequently associated with progressive CKD. COL4A3 p.(Gly407Arg) apparently confers a more penetrant renal phenotype. AD-AS demonstrates a continuum of phenotypes even among relatives, underscoring the importance of early identification, longitudinal monitoring, and renoprotective therapy.

articles.title: Maternal fish or n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid intake during pregnancy and risk of impaired kidney function at 6 years of age: the Japan environment and children's study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Chronic kidney disease in children causes kidney failure and growth impairment, making its prevention an urgent clinical and public health priority. Experimental animal studies have suggested that maternal intake of n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) during pregnancy may have kidney-protective effects in offspring; however, evidence in humans remains limited. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the association between maternal fish or n-3 PUFA intake during pregnancy and kidney dysfunction in children. METHODS: We analyzed data from the Japan Environment and Children's Study, a nationwide prospective birth cohort. A total of 2,679 mother-child pairs were included. Kidney dysfunction was defined as an estimated glomerular filtration rate < 90 mL/min/1.73 m² at 6 years of age. Maternal fish or n-3 PUFA intake during pregnancy was categorized into quintiles. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to estimate the associations. RESULTS: At 6 years of age, 262 children (9.8%) had decreased kidney function. In the adjusted model, maternal fish intake in the highest quintile was associated with a significantly lower risk of kidney dysfunction compared with the lowest quintile (odds ratio, 0.63; 95% confidence interval, 0.41-0.99). Maternal n-3 PUFA intake showed a similar trend, although the association was not statistically significant. CONCLUSION: Higher maternal fish intake during pregnancy was associated with a reduced risk of kidney dysfunction in offspring, whereas maternal n-3 PUFA intake showed no significant association. These findings suggest that higher maternal fish intake during pregnancy may be associated with a lower risk of impaired kidney function in children.

articles.title: Associations of Physical Activity With Mortality and Cardiovascular Diseases in Adults With Chronic Kidney Disease: A Community-Based Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is linked to elevated risks of mortality and cardiovascular diseases (CVDs). This study aimed to investigate the dose-response associations of moderate-to-vigorous-intensity physical activity (MVPA) with all-cause mortality and CVD risk in adults with CKD. METHODS: We included 3927 UK Biobank participants with CKD. Weekly MVPA duration was evaluated by wrist-worn accelerometers and a machine learning model. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and CVDs (heart failure, myocardial infarction, and stroke). Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic splines were used to assess the dose-response associations. RESULTS: CKD participants engaged in less MVPA than healthy controls. During a median follow-up of 7.92 years, 393 deaths and 445 CVDs occurred. Moderate-to-vigorous-intensity physical activity showed nonlinear associations with mortality and CVD risk. Mortality risk declined sharply up to 150 minutes per week MVPA and plateaued thereafter. Cardiovascular disease risk reached its lowest at approximately 300 minutes per week. Compared with <150 minutes per week, ≥150 minutes per week MVPA was associated with lower risks of mortality (hazard ratio = 0.64; 95% CI, 0.51-0.80) and CVDs (hazard ratio = 0.68; 95% CI, 0.55-0.83). Replacing sedentary behavior with MVPA for 10 min/d was associated with a significantly reduced mortality rate among less active CKD participants (hazard ratio = 0.70; 95% CI, 0.56-0.86). CONCLUSIONS: In adults with CKD, engaging in MVPA of ≥150 minutes per week was associated with significantly lower risks of mortality and CVDs. These findings underscore the value of physical activity promotion in CKD management.

articles.title: Micro-axial flow pump vs veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation for high-risk percutaneous coronary interventions: a randomized trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: The efficacy of prophylactic mechanical circulatory support with micro-axial flow pump or veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) in patients with severely reduced left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) undergoing high-risk percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remains unclear. METHODS: Patients with complex three-vessel disease, unprotected left main coronary disease or last patent conduit and LVEF ≤ 35% were assigned to receive either a micro-axial flow pump (SynFlow 3.0) or VA-ECMO support during a non-emergent high-risk PCI procedure in this prospective, multicentre, randomized, open-label, non-inferiority trial. The primary endpoint was the incidence of 30-day major adverse events, defined as any of: all-cause death, myocardial infarction, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, repeat revascularization, major bleeding, acute kidney injury, cardiopulmonary resuscitation/cardioversion, cardiac surgery/limb ischaemia, or serious device-related complications. Safety endpoints included adverse events and serious adverse events. RESULTS: The primary endpoint, 30-day major adverse events, occurred in 8 of 109 patients (7.34%) in the SynFlow 3.0 group and 13 of 113 patients (11.5%) in the VA-ECMO group (absolute difference adjusted for centre effect, -4.6%; 95% confidence interval, -12.6% to 3.5%; P for non-inferiority < .001). Patients with SynFlow 3.0 had shorter post-procedural hospital stay (4.1 days vs 5.2 days on average, P = .047) and fewer device-related adverse events (3.7% vs 11.5%; P = .041). Anaemia occurred more often with VA-ECMO than with SynFlow 3.0 (20.4% vs 9.2%; P = .023). CONCLUSIONS: The prophylactic use of a micro-axial flow pump during high-risk PCI procedures was non-inferior to VA-ECMO in the incidence of 30-day major adverse events. The use of a micro-axial flow pump was associated with shorter post-procedural hospital stay and fewer device-related adverse events.

articles.title: Perioperative dynamics of selenoproteins and risk of cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury.
articles.abstract: Cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury (CSA-AKI) affects over 20% of patients and is associated with perioperative mortality and long-term renal impairment. Reliable early biomarkers remain limited. Selenoproteins, including glutathione peroxidases (GPX1, GPX3) and selenoprotein P (SEPP1), are critical for redox homeostasis, but their perioperative changes in CSA-AKI remain unclear. This study aimed to characterize selenoprotein dynamics and explore their association with renal function and CSA-AKI. In this prospective observational cohort study, 99 adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery were enrolled, serum and urine samples were collected preoperatively and at 24/48 h postoperatively. SEPP1, GPX1, GPX3, and KIM-1 were measured. Mixed-effects, correlation, and logistic regression assessed selenoprotein dynamics and associations with CSA-AKI, with an exploratory model including age and preoperative SEPP1. Among 89 analyzed patients, 22 (24.7%) developed AKI. Univariable analyses showed that lower perioperative SEPP1 levels, attenuated urinary SEPP1 increases, and greater serum GPX1 decreases were associated with higher odds of CSA-AKI; older age, hypertension, and longer operation time were also associated with CSA-AKI. Postoperatively, serum SEPP1 declined markedly, remaining lower in AKI patients. Urinary SEPP1 increased significantly in non-AKI patients. Changes in GPX1 and GPX3 differed between AKI and non-AKI groups. Serum SEPP1 correlated positively with eGFR and inversely with creatinine and cystatin C. An exploratory model incorporating age and preoperative serum SEPP1 yielded an apparent AUC of 0.818. In summary, perioperative alterations in selenoproteins (GPX1, GPX3, SEPP1) are closely linked to CSA-AKI. Preoperative SEPP1 combined with clinical variables may enable early risk prediction and support timely intervention.

articles.title: Transportable early renal recovery phenotypes and 30-day major adverse kidney events after sepsis-associated acute kidney injury: A MIMIC-IV discovery and eICU-CRD external-validation cohort study.
articles.abstract: Early renal recovery after sepsis-associated acute kidney injury is heterogeneous. We aimed to derive clinically interpretable early recovery phenotypes, assess their transportability through fixed-centroid external assignment, and examine associations with 30-day major adverse kidney events (MAKE30). This retrospective discovery and external-validation cohort study used Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV and eICU-CRD. Eligible patients were adults with a first intensive care unit stay and Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes -compatible acute kidney injury within 7 days of sepsis onset. K-means clustering integrated five renal, fluid, and hemodynamic domains across twelve 6-hour intervals after acute kidney injury onset. Stability was assessed by repeated 80% patient subsampling. eICU CRD patients were assigned to fixed MIMIC-derived centroids without reclustering. Modified Poisson models estimated adjusted risk ratios (RRs). Of 9725 Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV patients with known MAKE30 status, 2529 (26.0%) experienced MAKE30. Four phenotypes were identified in 7965 patients: low-burden rapid-recovery, preserved-diuresis intermediate-risk, oliguric kidney-failure, and shock-vasopressor. The four-cluster solution had a median adjusted Rand index of 0.939 (empirical 2.5th-97.5th percentiles, 0.892-0.990). Relative to the low-burden phenotype, adjusted MAKE30 RRs were 1.74 (95% confidence interval , 1.58-1.90), 3.80 (3.47-4.16), and 3.68 (3.34-4.06). In eICU-CRD, 4708 of 8771 patients (53.7%) could be assigned; corresponding RRs were 2.82 (2.45-3.23), 4.78 (4.00-5.72), and 4.99 (4.32-5.76). Unassigned patients had higher MAKE30 rates than assigned patients (41.1% vs 25.2%). MAKE30 associations persisted in landmark and distance-restricted analyses. Early renal recovery trajectories identified four reproducible clinical phenotypes associated with MAKE30. Fixed-centroid assignment reproduced the direction of these associations in eICU-CRD patients with sufficient trajectory data. Selective assignment and the observational design limit generalizability and preclude conclusions about phenotype-guided treatment.

articles.title: Impact of ramadan fasting on bone mineral metabolism in hemodialysis: a multi-center prospective observational cohort study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: The effects of Ramadan fasting on biochemical parameters and bone mineral metabolism in maintenance hemodialysis (MHD) patients remain insufficiently studied. This study aimed to evaluate the impact of Ramadan fasting on biochemical indices and bone turnover biomarkers in patients undergoing chronic hemodialysis. METHODS: This multi-center prospective observational cohort study included 138 adult hemodialysis patients recruited from four dialysis centers in Dakahlia Governorate, Egypt. Eligible patients were aged 18-85 years, on stable hemodialysis for at least six months, and had no recent changes in treatments affecting mineral bone disease parameters. Patients were classified according to fasting behavior into three groups: non-fasting, fasting on non-dialysis days only, and fasting throughout Ramadan. Clinical data, dialysis characteristics, interdialytic weight gain, and intradialytic complications were recorded. Blood samples were obtained at the beginning and end of Ramadan to assess biochemical parameters and bone metabolism biomarkers, including alkaline phosphatase (ALP), bone-specific alkaline phosphatase (BSAP), fibroblast growth factor-23 (FGF23), sclerostin, α-Klotho, and tartrate-resistant acid phosphatase 5b (TRAP5b). Statistical comparisons of biochemical and bone-biomarker changes between baseline and post-Ramadan time points were performed among the three groups. RESULTS: Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were largely comparable among groups. No significant differences were observed in dialysis-related complications, including hypotension and hypoglycemia, before or after Ramadan. Serum potassium decreased to a comparable extent across all three groups, with no significant between-group difference, while serum sodium and albumin showed modest increases in patients fasting throughout Ramadan. Calcium, phosphorus, magnesium, and iPTH levels remained stable across groups. Among bone biomarkers, an unadjusted between-group difference in BSAP change was observed (P = 0.041), with an increase in non-fasting patients contrasting with stable or slightly decreased levels in fasting patients; this difference did not persist after adjustment for age, sex, BMI, and dialysis vintage (adjusted P = 0.229). FGF23, sclerostin, and TRAP5b increased, whereas Klotho decreased across all groups, with no significant between-group differences before or after adjustment. No clinically significant bone-related adverse events were reported. CONCLUSION: No short-term safety signal was detected in this selected, clinically stable hemodialysis cohort under medical supervision, although the study was not designed or powered to evaluate safety. Fasting was associated with stable biochemical parameters and a relatively stable bone turnover profile, without worsening mineral bone disease markers. Larger controlled studies with longer follow-up are needed to clarify the long-term skeletal effects of Ramadan fasting in this population.

articles.title: Clinical risk factors associated with acute hypertension-mediated organ damage in patients presenting with severe hypertension: A retrospective cohort study from Qatar.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe hypertension is a common reason for emergency department (ED) visits and is associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes. Identifying factors associated with acute hypertension-mediated organ damage (HMOD) may improve risk stratification. METHODS: A large retrospective cohort study across four hospitals in Qatar (January 2015-January 2020). Adults presenting to the ED with severe hypertension (systolic blood pressure [SBP] ≥ 180 mmHg and/or diastolic blood pressure [DBP] ≥ 110 mmHg) were included. In a cross-sectional primary analysis, the outcome was hypertensive emergency, defined as acute HMOD present at the index presentation, and univariable and multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with acute HMOD at presentation. A separate exploratory longitudinal secondary analysis described cardiovascular, cerebrovascular, and renal complications over three years of follow-up using descriptive statistics was conducted. Discrimination and calibration were assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and Hosmer-Lemeshow test. RESULTS: Of 881 patients (median age 50 years [IQR 43-57]; 68.8% male), 94.7% had severe asymptomatic hypertension and 5.3% presented with hypertensive emergency. Independent factors associated with acute HMOD were higher admission SBP (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 1.016, 95% CI 1.000-1.033), higher DBP (aOR 1.027, 95% CI 1.006-1.049), chronic kidney disease (aOR 2.38, 95% CI 1.02-5.57), hypertensive retinopathy (aOR 3.82, 95% CI 1.14-12.83), and current smoking (aOR 2.83, 95% CI 1.32-6.06). The model showed good discrimination (AUC 0.77) and adequate calibration. Kidney disease progression was the most common follow-up complication. CONCLUSIONS: Elevated admission blood pressure, chronic kidney disease, hypertensive retinopathy, and current smoking were independently associated with acute HMOD. These readily identifiable factors may support ED risk stratification in patients with severe hypertension.
articles.journal: Clinical and experimental hypertension (New York, N.Y. : 1993)

articles.title: Prevalence and prognostic significance of extrarenal manifestations in patients with lupus nephritis: A retrospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prevalence and prognostic implications of extrarenal involvement in lupus nephritis (LN), with emphasis on treatment response and the risk of future renal and extrarenal flares. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients newly diagnosed with LN between January 2006 and December 2022 and categorized them according to the presence of extrarenal involvement at diagnosis. Renal response and remission at 12 months, defined according to the Definition of Remission in SLE (DORIS), as well as the incidence of renal and extrarenal flares during follow-up, were compared between groups. Factors associated with DORIS remission and renal response were assessed using multivariable logistic regression analyses. RESULTS: Among 348 patients with LN, 156 (44.8%) had extrarenal involvement at diagnosis, most commonly hematological manifestations (59.0%). Rates of complete renal response (CRR) and DORIS remission at 12 months were comparable between patients with and without extrarenal involvement (CRR: 57.1% vs. 46.9%, p = 0.06; DORIS remission: 21.8% vs. 29.7%, p = 0.09). Over a median follow-up of 79.6 months, the incidence of renal flares (28.8% vs. 26.0%, p = 0.56) and extrarenal flares (26.3% vs. 24.5%, p = 0.74) did not differ significantly between groups. In multivariable analyses, baseline extrarenal involvement was not associated with DORIS remission (odds ratio [OR], 1.307; 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.779-2.193; p = 0.310) or renal response (OR, 0.974; 95% CI: 0.564-1.682; p = 0.925). CONCLUSIONS: Extrarenal involvement is present in nearly half of patients at LN diagnosis, however, it does not appear to influence renal response, DORIS remission, or the long-term risk of renal or extrarenal flares.

articles.title: Ravulizumab in IgA Nephropathy - Interim Analysis of a Phase 3 Trial.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: In patients with IgA nephropathy, complement activation drives glomerular inflammation, which leads to hematuria, proteinuria, and nephron loss. Ravulizumab is a terminal complement inhibitor that prevents formation of C5a and C5b-9. METHODS: In this phase 3 trial, we enrolled adults with IgA nephropathy who had an estimated glomerular filtration rate of at least 30 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and proteinuria (24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio [with protein and creatinine both measured in grams] of ≥0.75 or total urinary protein excretion of ≥1.0 g per day), despite standard therapy. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive an intravenous infusion of either ravulizumab or placebo every 8 weeks. In the prespecified interim analysis, the primary efficacy end point was the change from baseline in the 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at week 34. Safety was also assessed. RESULTS: In all, 485 patients underwent randomization, with 240 patients assigned to the ravulizumab group and 245 to the placebo group; 352 patients (176 in each group) were included in the interim analysis. In the ravulizumab group, the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio at baseline and at week 34 was 1.56 and 0.83, respectively; in the placebo group, it was 1.60 and 1.48, respectively. At week 34, a significant reduction in the geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio was observed with ravulizumab (-46.6%) as compared with the reduction observed with placebo (-5.6%), corresponding to an adjusted geometric mean 24-hour urinary protein-to-creatinine ratio that was 43.4% (99% confidence interval, 30.1 to 54.2) lower with ravulizumab than with placebo (P<0.001). Adverse events occurred in 69.5% of the patients receiving ravulizumab and in 75.8% of those receiving placebo; serious adverse events occurred in 4.6% and 9.0%, respectively. No meningococcal infections or deaths occurred. CONCLUSIONS: In adults with IgA nephropathy, ravulizumab resulted in a significantly greater reduction in the protein-to-creatinine ratio than placebo at week 34. (Funded by Alexion, AstraZeneca Rare Disease Unit; I CAN ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06291376; EU Clinical Trials number, 2023-507851-31-00.).
articles.journal: The New England journal of medicine

articles.title: Sex differences in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: the FINE-HEART pooled analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: While the prevalence, drivers, and impact of cardiometabolic risk factors are known to differ between women and men, less is known about sex differences in the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome. METHODS: In this prespecified analysis, individual participant-level data were pooled from two trials of chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes (FIDELIO-DKD and FIGARO-DKD) and a trial of heart failure (HF) with mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction (FINEARTS-HF). The risk of first HF hospitalization, cardiovascular death, major adverse cardiovascular events, kidney composite outcome, and all-cause death, was compared between men and women using adjusted Cox regression models. Treatment effect heterogeneity in response to finerenone was evaluated using interaction analyses. RESULTS: Of the 18 991 participants in FINE-HEART, 6664 (35%) were women. Compared with men, women were slightly older (69 vs 67 years) and had a lower median urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (183 vs 337 mg/g). Women were more likely to have Stage 4 CKM syndrome but less likely to receive medical therapies commonly indicated for the management of CKM conditions at baseline, such as aspirin, statins, renin-angiotensin system inhibitors, sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 inhibitors, and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists. During a median follow-up of 2.9 years, both women and men had similarly high rates of HF hospitalization or cardiovascular death (4.8 vs 3.9 per 100 patient-years, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 0.97, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.89-1.06, P = .52) but lower risk of all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.76-0.91, P < .001) compared with men. There was no evidence of treatment heterogeneity by sex with finerenone in reducing cardiovascular, kidney, and mortality outcomes (all Pinteraction >.05). CONCLUSIONS: In this pooled analysis of individuals with advanced CKM syndrome, women had a higher burden of multimorbidity and were less likely to receive commonly indicated CKM therapies than men. Finerenone conferred consistent benefits in women and men, reinforcing its use while underscoring persistent sex-based treatment disparities in CKM care. REGISTRATION: PROSPERO identifier: CRD42024570467.

articles.title: Spatial transcriptomics tumor microenvironment determinants of tyrosine kinase inhibitor response in renal cell carcinoma: results from a phase 2 clinical trial.
articles.abstract: Metastatic clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) exhibits heterogeneous clinical outcomes, and limited biomarkers are available to predict response to targeted therapies. This study evaluated cell compartment-specific transcriptional biomarkers predicting clinical response to the tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) sunitinib. In this phase 2 clinical trial (NCT00715442), 46 patients with metastatic ccRCC received sunitinib pre- and post-cytoreductive nephrectomy, with a primary endpoint of time-to-progression (TTP) and secondary endpoints of overall survival (OS) and sunitinib toxicity. To investigate spatial dynamics of therapeutic response to sunitinib, we applied whole-transcriptome digital spatial profiling (DSP) to tumor tissue from responders and non-responders. For 46 trial patients, median TTP was 8.2 months (95% CI: 6.1-19.3) and OS 36.3 months (95% CI: 19.7-70.5). Responders displayed a tumor microenvironment enriched in pro-inflammatory/immunostimulatory programs, while non-responders displayed enrichment of immunosuppressive programs with elevated PD-L1 expression in myeloid cells and exhausted CD8 + T-cell signatures. Sunitinib resistance mechanisms involving VEGF-dependent and independent angiogenic pathways were identified, revealing potential therapeutic targets. DSP-based machine learning models showed strong prognostic and predictive performance in sunitinib-treated patients in an external JAVELIN Renal 101 cohort, but attenuated performance in the avelumab plus axitinib cohort, indicating treatment-context specificity. Our findings highlight immune regulation as a key determinant of sunitinib response in metastatic ccRCC. Spatial profiling revealed potentially targetable mechanisms of TKI resistance involving SPP1-associated myeloid programs, CD8 + T-cell exhaustion, and angiogenic signaling, highlighting interactions between angiogenesis, lipid metabolism, and tumor immunity as determinants of therapeutic outcome.

articles.title: Association of obstructive sleep apnea with outcomes in hospitalized patients with pneumonia: a retrospective analysis of the nationwide inpatient sample.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) impairs mucociliary defense, reduces ventilatory reserve, promotes systemic inflammation, and predisposes patients to lower respiratory tract infections. Despite biological plausibility, the population-level association of comorbid OSA with pneumonia hospitalization outcomes remains poorly characterized. We aimed to evaluate associations between OSA and clinical outcomes in adults hospitalized with pneumonia using a nationally representative inpatient database. METHODS: Using the 2018-2020 Nationwide Inpatient Sample (NIS), we conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults (≥ 18 years) hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of pneumonia, stratified by OSA status. Multivariable logistic and linear regression models adjusted for age, sex, race/ethnicity, household income quartile, primary payer, Charlson Comorbidity Index, obesity, hospital type, hospital bed size, and geographic region. P-values were corrected for multiple comparisons (Bonferroni), and E-values were calculated to assess sensitivity to unmeasured confounding. RESULTS: Among 4,918,328 hospitalizations, 9.2% (n = 450,580) had coexisting OSA. Despite a greater comorbidity burden, OSA was associated with lower in-hospital mortality (3.3% vs. 4.8%; aOR 0.74; 95% CI 0.71-0.77; p < 0.0001), lower sepsis (aOR 0.89; 95% CI 0.87-0.90), and lower septic shock (2.2% vs. 2.7%; aOR 0.80; 95% CI 0.76-0.84). Conversely, OSA was associated with higher acute respiratory failure (48.1% vs. 35.8%; aOR 1.56; 95% CI 1.54-1.59), noninvasive ventilation (NIV) use (14.8% vs. 5.0%; aOR 3.26; 95% CI 3.17-3.34), and acute kidney injury (AKI; 24.1% vs. 22.1%; aOR 1.13; 95% CI 1.11-1.15). Adjusted length of stay was slightly longer (β + 0.11 days; 95% CI 0.07-0.16), while adjusted hospital charges did not differ significantly. All associations except hospital charges remained significant after correction for multiple comparisons; E-values suggested that the sepsis and AKI associations could be explained by relatively weak unmeasured confounding. CONCLUSIONS: Among adults hospitalized with pneumonia, comorbid OSA was associated with higher rates of acute respiratory failure, NIV use, and AKI, and with lower in-hospital mortality and sepsis. Because of the retrospective administrative design and the lack of data on pneumonia severity, OSA severity, and CPAP use, residual and unmeasured confounding cannot be excluded. These findings are hypothesis-generating, and prospective studies are needed.
